feed.title: Thoughts on a network policy for quantum-vulnerable UTXOs (long-exposure quantum attacks)

entry.title: Thoughts on a network policy for quantum-vulnerable UTXOs (long-exposure quantum attacks)
entry.summary:
Advancements in cryptography and the looming threat of cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) have raised pressing concerns about the security of Bitcoin addresses, particularly those using BIP32 derivation. By prohibiting spending based solely on elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) signatures and introducing a zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) based recovery mechanism, it becomes feasible to protect BTC held by procrastinators who have not yet migrated their funds from vulnerable BIP32 addresses. This approach would safeguard against potential theft resulting from CRQC attacks.
However, implementing such protective measures is not without consequences. Addresses created before BIP32, particularly pay-to-public-key (P2PK) types and a small subset of non-standardly derived addresses, would effectively be confiscated under this model, since they do not benefit from the ZKP escape hatch. To reduce the impact of this confiscation, there is an option to permit either time-restricted (hour-glass) or unrestricted spending from P2PK addresses, acknowledging that these older formats may not be salvageable through zero-knowledge proofs. The ethical and philosophical implications of such selective protection are contentious, with some considering the forfeiture of legacy coins difficult to accept.
The appropriate course of action largely depends on timing and the scale of affected users. If CRQC capabilities emerge before post-quantum (PQ) secure addresses are widely adopted in Bitcoin, disabling ECC-based spending becomes unavoidable. Conversely, if only a negligible number of coins are at risk, consensus for sweeping protocol changes may not materialize. For scenarios where agreement cannot be reached, an alternative proposal has been outlined for actively sweeping vulnerable outputs after so-called Q-day. More details on this plan can be found at [Active Sweeping of Vulnerable Outputs After Q-Day](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/active-sweeping-of-vulnerable-outputs-after-q-day/2421).
